question.text: Diversification benefits from combining two assets are maximised when the correlation between the assets is:

explanation.text: The Logic: The lower the correlation between two assets, the greater the diversification benefit. At a correlation of -1, complete diversification benefits can be realised: a suitably weighted combination of the two assets can produce a portfolio with zero risk. The Trap: A correlation of +1 means the two assets move identically and provide no diversification benefit. Correlations of +0.5 and 0 still provide some diversification benefit, but neither permits a zero-risk combination the way perfect negative correlation does. Note: Correlation runs from -1 to +1, and diversification benefit increases as the correlation moves lower. Only at -1 can a properly weighted two-asset portfolio be constructed with zero risk.
